title: Review: Centripetal force; Simple harmonic motion: definition and graphs; Mass–spring and pendulum; Damping, forced oscillations and resonance
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: O01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; O04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; O04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; O01-uk1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C02-1#N.3a, O01-1#N.11, O01-uk1#N.6, O02-1#N.4c, O04-1#N.10a, C02-1#N.4a, O02-1#N.7c, O04-1#N.2a, C02-1#N.15, O04-1#N.4a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Equilibrium position
items.clue: Place where an oscillating object would rest; the restoring force is zero there.

items.label: Natural frequency
items.clue: Symbol f₀: cycles per second of a system that is displaced, let go and left alone.

items.label: Free oscillation
items.clue: Motion after a system is displaced and released, with nothing further acting on it.

items.label: Phase difference
items.clue: Angle 2π × Δt/T, where Δt separates matching points of two oscillators with equal T.

questions.stem: A cyclist rides around a flat circular track at a constant speed of 8.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about her motion is correct?

options.text: Her velocity is constant, so the resultant force acting on her is zero.
Her velocity changes, so a resultant force acts towards the centre.
A resultant force acts on her outwards, away from the centre of the track.
A resultant force acts on her forwards, along her direction of motion.

questions.stem: A pendulum bob swings to and fro in a small arc. At the lowest point of its swing, what are its acceleration along its path and its speed?

options.text: Acceleration along the path greatest; speed zero.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed greatest.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed also zero.
Acceleration along the path greatest; speed greatest.

questions.explanation: The lowest point is equilibrium: the restoring force along the path is zero there. The bob sped up all the way down and starts to slow on the way up, so its speed is greatest here.

questions.stem: An object in SHM is released from rest at x = +0.060 m at time t = 0 and oscillates about x = 0 with a period of 1.2 s. What is the object's position at t = 0.20 s?

A trolley hung from a newton meter gives a reading of 14.7 N. The trolley is then attached to a spring system on a horizontal track and oscillates with negligible friction. The spring constant of the system is 7.50 N m⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the time period of the oscillation?
A singer shatters a wine glass by singing one steady note close to it. Which condition is essential for this to happen?

options.text: The note is very loud, whatever frequency the singer chooses.
The note is the highest frequency that the singer is able to produce.
The note's frequency is equal to a natural frequency of the glass.
The sound echoes inside the bowl of the glass and builds up.

questions.stem: A car travels at constant speed around a bend on a flat horizontal road; its path is part of a horizontal circle. Air resistance is negligible. Which statement about the horizontal forces on the car is correct?

options.text: Friction from the road acts towards the centre and is the resultant force.
Friction acts towards the centre and is balanced by a centrifugal force.
Friction and a separate centripetal force both act towards the centre.
A forward driving force along the bend is the resultant force on the car.

questions.stem: A long simple pendulum hangs in the stairwell of a school. Swinging with a small amplitude, its bob takes 2.10 s to move from one extreme position to the other. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the length of the pendulum?

A lightly damped mass–spring system has a natural frequency of 2.0 Hz. It is driven by a periodic force of constant amplitude with a frequency of 3.5 Hz. Which describes its oscillation once the amplitude has become steady?

options.text: At 3.5 Hz, with a smaller amplitude than when driven at 2.0 Hz
At 2.0 Hz, its natural frequency, with a small steady amplitude
At 3.5 Hz, with a larger amplitude than when it is driven at 2.0 Hz
At 3.5 Hz, with the same amplitude as when it is driven at 2.0 Hz

questions.stem: A car drives at constant speed over the top of a rounded hill in the road. Near the top, the road's vertical cross-section is a circular arc. The car stays in contact with the road. At the top, how does the normal force from the road compare with the car's weight?

options.text: It equals the weight, since at the top the car moves neither up nor down.
It is greater than the weight, as when the car drives through a dip.
It is less than the weight, so the forces on it add to a downward force.
It equals the weight plus mv²/r, to balance an outward force.

questions.explanation: The centre of the arc is below the car, so the forces must add up to mv²/r downwards: weight − normal force = mv²/r. The normal force is less than the weight by mv²/r.

questions.stem: In its spin cycle, a washing machine's drum speeds up steadily. At one rotation rate the whole machine shakes violently; at higher rates it runs smoothly again. Why does it shake at that one rate?

options.text: It is then rotating fastest, so it transfers the most energy per second.
The rotation rate then equals a natural frequency of the machine.
The damping in the machine's mounts falls to zero at that rotation rate.
It is no longer forced: the machine now oscillates freely at its own frequency.

questions.explanation: The spinning drum drives the machine. When the driving frequency matches a natural frequency, energy builds up each cycle: resonance, maximum amplitude.
